questions.question: In a school, there are 200 students. If the ratio of the number of boys and the number of girls is 9 ∶ 1, then find the mean proportion between the number of boys and that of girls in the school.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Total number of students = 200

Ratio of boys to girls = 9 : 1

**Concept used: **

The mean proportional between two quantities is the square root of the product of the two quantities.

**Solution:**

Number of boys = 9/10 × 200 = 180

Number of girls = 1/10 × 200 = 20

Mean Proportional = √(180 × 20) = √3600 = 60

**Therefore, the mean proportion between the number of boys and that of girls in the school is 60.**

questions.question: Which number should be subtracted from 17, 30, 22 and 40 so that the obtained numbers may become proportional?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Numbers: 17, 30, 22, 40

**Concept used:**

The concept of proportion.

**Solution:**

Let the number to be subtracted be x.

So, the numbers after subtraction will be 17 - x, 30 - x, 22 - x, 40 - x.

According to the concept of proportion, (30-x)/(17-x) = (40-x)/(22-x).

⇒ (30-x) × (22-x) = (40-x) × (17-x)

⇒ 660 - 52x = 680 - 57x

⇒ x = 4.

**Therefore, 4 should be subtracted from 17, 30, 22, and 40 so that the obtained numbers may become proportional.**

questions.question: A man purchased two items at the same price and sold one at a profit of 15% and the other at a loss of 5%. If the difference between the two selling prices is ₹80, then what is the cost price of one item?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Difference in selling prices = ₹80

Profit on one item = 15%

Loss on the other item = 5%

**Concept used: **

Profit/loss percentage formula.

**Solution:**

Let the cost price be x.

Selling price of the first item = x + 15% of x = 1.15x

Selling price of the second item = x - 5% of x = 0.95x

The difference in selling prices = 1.15x - 0.95x = 0.2x = ₹80

Solving for x, x = ₹80 / 0.2 = ₹400

**Therefore, the cost price of one item is ₹400.**

questions.question:
A company offers different types of discounts schemes.

(i) Two successive discounts of 10% and 20%

(ii) Buy 1 get 1 free

(iii) Buy 5 get 3 free

(iv) Buy 5 get 6

Which scheme has the minimum discount percentage?
questions.solution:
**Given data:**

Two successive discounts of 10% and 20%

Buy 1 get 1 free

Buy 5 get 3 free

Buy 5 get 6

**Concept used: **Calculation of effective discount percentage.

**Solution:**

Effective discount of two successive discounts of 10% and 20% = 10% + 20% - (10% × 20%) = 28%

Discount for Buy 1 get 1 free = 50%

Discount for Buy 5 get 3 free = (3/8) × 100 = 37.5%

Discount for Buy 5 get 6 = (1/6) × 100 = 16.66%

**Therefore, the scheme (iv) Buy 5 get 6 has a minimum discount percentage of 16.66%.**

questions.question: A thief noticing a policeman from a distance of 500 metres starts running at a speed of 8 km/h. The policeman chased him with a speed of 11 km/h. What is the distance run by the thief before he was caught? (Rounded off to two decimal places, if required)
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Initial distance between thief and policeman = 500 m

Speed of thief = 8 km/h

Speed of policeman = 11 km/h

**Concept used:**

Relative speed and time = distance/speed

**Solution:**

Relative speed = speed of policeman - speed of thief = 11 km/h - 8 km/h = 3 km/h = 3 × (1000/3600) m/s = 5/6 m/s

Time taken to catch the thief = initial distance / relative speed 

Time taken to catch the thief = 500 m / (5/6 m/s) = 600 seconds

Distance run by the thief before he was caught = Speed of thief × time = (8 × 1000/3600) m/s × 600 s = 1333.33 meters

**Therefore, the distance run by the thief before he was caught is approximately 1333.33 meters.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__** 

Here, the thief and the police is running for the same time. So, time = constant.

When time is constant Speed ∝ Distance

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/be3bfa3988ecc59d9297569f46f971cd5b20fee354f868f4543e674f9fc76082.png] 

Distance between the thief and the police = 3 unit = 500 km

⇒ 1 unit = 500/3 

⇒ 8 unit = (500 × 8)/3 = 1333.33 m

Therefore, the distance run by the thief before he was caught is approximately 1333.33 meters.

questions.question: A person buys the stock of a company at Rs. 12,000. If he sells that stock (a year later) he gets Rs. 15,000. Determine the percentage profit earned.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Purchase price of stock = Rs. 12,000

Selling price of stock = Rs. 15,000

**Concept used: **

Calculation of profit percentage = (Profit/Cost Price) x 100%

**Solution:**

Profit = Selling Price - Cost Price = Rs. 15,000 - Rs. 12,000 = Rs. 3,000

Profit Percentage = (Profit / Cost Price) x 100% = (Rs. 3,000 / Rs. 12,000) x 100% = 25%

**Therefore, the percentage profit earned is 25%.**

questions.question: The curved surface area of a right circular cylinder is 90.2 m², and its radius is 70 cm, find its height (in m). Take π = (22)/(7)
questions.solution:
**Given data:**

Curved surface area of a right circular cylinder = 90.2 m²

Radius of the cylinder = 70 cm = 0.7 m

π = 22/7

**Concept used: **

Formula for the curved surface area of a cylinder is 2πrh

**Solution:**

Using the formula 2πrh = 90.2 m², we can solve for h.

Substituting the given values, we get 2 × (22/7) × 0.7 × h = 90.2

Solving for h, h = 90.2 / (2 × (22/7) × 0.7) = 20.5 m

**Therefore, the height of the cylinder is 20.5 m.**

questions.question: A park had an average of 30 children playing on weekdays and an average of 60 children playing on weekends. Find the average number of children playing per day in the park for the month of June beginning with a Saturday.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Average of 30 children playing on weekdays

Average of 60 children playing on weekends

**Concept used: **

Calculation of overall average.

**Solution:**

Total number of children playing on weekdays in June = 30 × 20 = 600 (as June has 20 weekdays)

Total number of children playing on weekends in June = 60 × 10 = 600 (as June has 10 weekends)

Total number of children playing in June = 600 + 600 = 1200

Average number of children playing per day = Total number of children / Total days = 1200 / 30 = 40

**Therefore, the average number of children playing per day in the park for June is 40.

questions.question: The population of a town 3 years ago was 84000. Due to migration to cities, it decreases every year at the rate of 10 percent. The present population of the town is :
questions.solution:
**Given data:**

Initial population of the town = 84000

Rate of decrease = 10%

**Concept used: **The formula for compound decrease.

**Solution:**

Current population = Initial population × (1 - rate/100)time

Substituting the given values, we get 84000 × (1 - 10/100)³ = 63504

⇒ 84000 × (9/10)3 = 61236

**Therefore, the present population of the town is approximately 61236.**

questions.question: The average income of 74 persons is Rs. 5,200 and that of a manager is Rs. 6,000. Then the average income of the whole group is (consider up to two decimals):
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Average income of 74 persons = Rs. 5,200

Manager's income = Rs. 6,000

**Concept used: **

Calculation of overall average.

**Solution:**

Total income of 74 persons = 74 × 5200 = Rs. 384,800

Total income of the whole group = 384,800 + 6,000 = Rs. 390,800

The average income of the whole group = Total income / Total people = 390,800 / 75 = Rs. 5210.66

**Therefore, the average income of the whole group is Rs. 5210.66.**

questions.question: The least value of 'a' for which the number 638a435 is completely divisible by 3 is:
questions.solution:
**Given data:**

Number = 638a435

**Concept used: **

Rule of divisibility by 3. A number is divisible by 3 if the sum of its digits is divisible by 3.

**Solution:**

Sum of digits = 6 + 3 + 8 + a + 4 + 3 + 5 = 29 + a

For the number to be divisible by 3, a must be 1 (because 29 + 1 = 30 is divisible by 3)

**Therefore, the least value of 'a' for which the number 638a435 is completely divisible by 3 is 1.**

questions.question: In an exam, a student scored 40% on the first paper out of a total of 200. How much percentage should the student score in the second paper out of 200 if he has to get 60% marks overall?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since both papers carry equal maximum marks (200 each), the overall percentage is simply the average of the individual percentages.

Overall % = (Paper 1 % + Paper 2 %) ÷ 2

60% = (40% + Paper 2 %) ÷ 2

120% = 40% + Paper 2 % ⇒ Paper 2 % = 80%

**∴ The correct answer is 80%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b59b5569fbb3ba6d3889bd191f15c2817276de43c6fe769a6d90e4f6d0af4e58.png] 

**Given:**

Maximum marks for Paper 1 = 200

Maximum marks for Paper 2 = 200

Overall target percentage required = 60%

**Calculation:**

⇒ Marks obtained in Paper 1 = (40 ÷ 100) × 200 = 80 marks

⇒ Total maximum marks for both papers = 200 + 200 = 400

⇒ Target marks required overall = (60 ÷ 100) × 400 = 240 marks

⇒ Marks required in Paper 2 = Target marks required − Marks in Paper 1

⇒ Marks required in Paper 2 = 240 − 80 = 160 marks

⇒ Percentage required in Paper 2 = (160 ÷ 200) × 100

⇒ Percentage required = 80%

**∴ The correct answer is 80%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Percentage (Equal Base)

When calculating overall percentages for components with equal total bases, the combined percentage is strictly the simple average: Combined % = (P₁ + P₂) ÷ 2.

Weighted Average (Unequal Base)

If the total marks are unequal (say W₁ and W₂), the weighted average method is required: Overall % = (W₁P₁ + W₂P₂) ÷ (W₁ + W₂).

Percentage to Absolute Value

To convert any percentage to absolute marks, use the standard formula: Value = (Percentage ÷ 100) × Total Base.

questions.question: A and B can finish a work in 15 days and 10 days, respectively. A started the work alone and after 5 days, B joined A in the work. They both did the remaining work. What is the total number of days to complete the work?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A can finish work in 15 days.

B can finish the same work in 10 days.

A started the work alone and after 5 days, B joined.

**Concept used: **

Calculation of work done based on time taken to complete it.

**Solution:**

A’s 1 day’s work = 1/15

B’s 1 day’s work = 1/10

Work done by A in 5 days = 5 × (1/15) = 1/3

Remaining work = 1 - 1/3 = 2/3

(A + B)’s 1 day's work = 1/15 + 1/10 = 1/6

Time taken by A and B together to complete the remaining work = (2/3) / (1/6) = 4 days

Total time taken = time taken by A alone + time taken by A and B together = 5 days + 4 days = 9 days

**Therefore, the total number of days to complete the work is 9 days.**

questions.question: If Ramesh walks at a speed of 15 km/h, instead of 12 km/h, he would have walked 2 km more in the same time. What is the actual distance (in km) travelled by Ramesh at 12 km/h in the same time?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Ramesh's normal speed = 12 km/h

Ramesh's increased speed = 15 km/h

Distance increased due to increased speed = 2 km

**Concept used: **

The concept of speed, time, and distance.

**Solution:**

Let's denote the time Ramesh spent walking as 't'.

Distance covered at normal speed = Speed × Time = 12t

Distance covered at increased speed = Speed × Time = 15t

According to the question, 15t = 12t + 2

Solving for 't', we get t = 2 / 3 hours

Substituting 't' back into the distance equation, Distance = 12t = 12 × 2/3 = 8 km

**Therefore, the actual distance travelled by Ramesh at 12 km/h in the same time is 8 km.**

questions.question: The smallest number exactly divisible by 104, 78 and 260 is P. If P + 40 = Q², then what is the positive value of Q?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Divisors are 104, 78, and 260

**Concept used: **

Least Common Multiple (LCM) and quadratic equations.

**Solution:**

The least number exactly divisible by 104, 78, and 260 is the LCM of these three numbers.

The LCM of 104, 78, and 260 is 1560.

Therefore, P = 1560

The problem states that P + 40 = Q². Substituting P into this equation gives 1560 + 40 = Q², so Q² = 1600

Solving for Q gives Q = 40 (we only take the positive root because Q represents a real number in this context).

**Therefore, the positive value of Q is 40.**
